closed.content: Tests in atlas are run through cargo nextest run; plain cargo test is not used.
The atlas test suite is run with cargo nextest run, not cargo test.
To ship atlas you run the bin/ship.sh script at the top of the repo.
Project atlas is deployed by running bin/ship.sh from the repository root.
Deploying atlas means executing bin/ship.sh; the old make deploy target is gone.
The branch under review is spike/consolidate.
The flaky test being chased this week is pagination_ordering in atlas-api.

Went through the full atlas memory set (117 live claims) using the consolidate tool, which does full pairwise comparison rather than a keyword search. Here's what I did and found:

**Merged (true duplicates, now single claims with history preserved via `supersedes`):**
- Three claims that all said "atlas deploys via `bin/ship.sh` from the repo root" (one of them also noting the old `make deploy` target is gone) → collapsed into one claim.
- Two claims that both said "tests run via `cargo nextest run`, not `cargo test`" → collapsed into one.

**Forgotten (stale scratch notes, not durable facts):**
- "The branch under review is spike/consolidate." — a session-scoped note, 40 days idle, well past its intended "fast decay" lifetime.
- "The flaky test being chased this week is pagination_ordering in atlas-api." — same, a "this week" note that outlived its relevance.

**Left alone — false positives:** The consolidate pass also flagged a bunch of pairs that share vocabulary ("atlas", "docs", "billing", "db") but are actually distinct facts, not duplicates — e.g. connection-pool-size vs readiness-probe-behavior, GHCR image push vs distroless base image, retention-policy-doc-location vs mdbook-publishing. I checked each and left these as-is since merging them would lose information.

**One real contradiction I did *not* resolve — needs your call:** two claims about atlas feature flags disagree:
- "Feature flags in atlas are an environment variable map and nothing more."
- "Feature flags in atlas are additive only, so `cargo check --all-features` has to pass."

These could be describing two different things (runtime env-var toggles vs. Cargo compile-time feature gates) or one could just be wrong/outdated. I didn't want to guess and silently overwrite a real fact — let me know which is current (or if both apply to different systems) and I'll update memory accordingly.
